task: Phase 2A Task 2S -- electrical gauge versus interface-continuity audit
supersedes: PHASE_02A_TASK2R gauge justification (rank-gain argument withdrawn as vacuous)
PHASE_02A_TASK2R normal-incidence amplitudes (per-side dimensionless scaling defect)

summary.question: Is the Task 2R row removal equivalent to a properly gauge-fixed full formulation, or does it merely solve?
summary.answer: EQUIVALENT -- but NOT for the reason Task 2R gave.
why_equivalent: The potential of a polynomial mode diverges like 1/k as k->0 (measured 2.63e11 at k/k_ac=1e-2 rising by exactly 100x per decade), so there is no k=0 value of phi to impose continuity on. The k=0 potential condition is a LIMIT.
At k=0 the Dz row is Gauss law D_z=0, which is the INSULATED interface condition. Imposing it on the bonded contact the rest of the system imposes would mix two electrical models.
The reduced k=0 answer IS the k->0 limit of the full answer, verified by extrapolation in k rather than assumed.
summary.why_task2r_reason_withdrawn: Task 2R argued the phi row adds no rank, therefore is implied. Measured: an ARBITRARY appended row also adds no rank once rows>=columns and columns are independent. Zero rank gain cannot distinguish a redundant row from an inconsistent one.
summary.equivalence_scope: 4 material pairs x {P,SV} x k/k_ac in {1e-2,1e-4}; gauge-invariant components only (phi excluded as the allowed gauge constant)

gauge_count.phi_row_rank_gain_note: reported for completeness; measured vacuous as proof -- see EQ-02A-GAUGE-03

production_defects.title: interface continuity rows built from per-side dimensionless states
production_defects.detail: Side.states divides by EACH medium own reference scales. Scale ratios Al6061 vs PZT-5H at k=0: theta 2.46881, txz 0.738449, tzz 0.597113, qz 178.461, Dz 2.46731e-13, phi 5.58798e-10. Subtracting them is not a continuity condition for dissimilar media.
production_defects.measured_before: Al|PZT SV k=0: matrix residual 2.296e-41 while PHYSICAL continuity violated by 0.2616
production_defects.fix: code/scattering/assembly.py builds columns and rhs from raw_states; code/scattering/solver.py reconstructs from raw_states

production_defects.title: column normalisation by the Euclidean norm over mixed physical units
production_defects.detail: Columns carry SI quantities spanning 1e-37 (D_z) to 1e22 (q_z). The Euclidean norm is dominated by q_z, so u_x=1 becomes 1e-14 and genuinely distinct columns score a Cauchy-Schwarz overlap of 1.0.
production_defects.measured_before: Al|PZT SV: Al shear mode u_x/|col|=1.88e-14 vs PZT 1.20e-14; both columns reported overlap 1.0
production_defects.measured_after: per-field row scale + per-mode column scale: cond 6.9-1.3e10, rank full at every precision
production_defects.fix: diagonal row+column equilibration, both invertible so the solution set is unchanged

production_defects.title: kernel-level truncation of the potential at k=0 in the full formulation
production_defects.detail: full_system assembled at exactly k=0 although the potential entry diverges like 1/k there, producing a k=0 answer that is not the limit.
production_defects.measured_before: Al|PZT P: full k=0 trans t_zz/inc t_zz = 1.3316249147+0.00115753873j versus the k->0 limit 1.3317978953
production_defects.measured_after: full_system now refuses k=0 with an explanatory ValueError; reduced_system gives 1.33179789533, matching the limit

task2s_tests.purpose: row 2 of the normal-incidence system is Gauss's law, and with the k*D_x term dropped at k = 0 it reads D_z = 0
task2s_tests.oracle: E_z = -i*xi*phi and D_z = e31*e_xx + e33*e_zz + eps33*E_z + p*theta rebuilt directly from the state vector
task2s_tests.expected: every physical mode satisfies i*xi*D_z = 0 to 1e-25, and the constitutive rebuild agrees to 1e-15 of the largest cancelled term
task2s_tests.tol_justification: two different things are measured. The structural identity holds to rounding. The constitutive rebuild is a CANCELLATION identity whose floor is set by the null vector's own accuracy -- measured 2.1e-17 against terms of order 1e7 -- so 1e-15 is the observed ceiling, not a convenience
task2s_tests.actual: |i*xi*D_z| = 3.353e-47 (Gauss's law at k=0 is D_z = 0); constitutive rebuild agrees to 2.126e-17 of the largest cancelled term over 6 modes
task2s_tests.detail: the null vector satisfies D_z = 0 to rounding, and the constitutive substitution reproduces it only to the cancellation floor -- which is why D_z = 0 is NOT an independent equation at k = 0

task2s_tests.purpose: count the gauge freedom: two constants per interface, one global invariance, therefore exactly one fixing condition
task2s_tests.oracle: the xi = 0 mode vector, which must be (0,0,1,0,0,0,0,0) -- a pure potential with no mechanical or thermal content
task2s_tests.fixture: all four material pairs, both polarisations, k = 1e-4*k_ac
task2s_tests.expected: one global gauge condition for every configuration, and the xi=0 vector is a pure potential
task2s_tests.tol_justification: exact structural property; the xi=0 entries are computed to rounding
task2s_tests.actual: 1 global gauge condition and a pure-potential xi=0 sector in every configuration
task2s_tests.detail: the xi=0 mode is read off the state, not asserted

task2s_tests.purpose: show that zero rank gain is vacuous as a proof of implication, so Task 2R's justification is withdrawn and replaced
task2s_tests.oracle: a deliberately INCONSISTENT extra row must also show zero rank gain; if it does, the test cannot detect implication
task2s_tests.fixture: Al6061|PZT-5H at k = 0, and the same system with a corrupted row that is certainly not implied
task2s_tests.expected: the corrupted row shows the same zero rank gain as the phi row, demonstrating the test has no power
task2s_tests.tol_justification: structural: rank is compared exactly between two matrices that differ only in one row
task2s_tests.actual: an arbitrary appended row also gains 0 rank, so rank gain cannot certify implication: Al6061|Al6061 P: gain=0; Al6061|Al6061 SV: gain=0; PZT-5H|PZT-5H P: gain=0; PZT-5H|PZT-5H SV: gain=0
task2s_tests.detail: a row of constants cannot be implied by the interface equations, yet it is rank-neutral exactly like phi

task2s_tests.purpose: the gauge-fixed full system and the reduced system produce the same physical fields at k > 0, for all four pairs
task2s_tests.oracle: two independently assembled systems -- the full one carries explicit constants C_1,C_2 and a gauge-fixing row, the reduced one carries neither
task2s_tests.fixture: Al|Al, PZT|PZT, Al|PZT, PZT|Al at k/k_ac = 1e-2 and 1e-4, P and SV
task2s_tests.expected: transmitted/incident transfer ratios agree to 1e-40 for u_x, u_z, theta, t_xz, t_zz, D_z and q_z
task2s_tests.tol_justification: 60-digit arithmetic, both systems conditioned below 1e11 after row and column equilibration; measured worst disagreement 1.7e-48
task2s_tests.actual: worst gauge-invariant disagreement = 2.07e-48 at PZT-5H|Al6061 SV k=1e-4 qz
task2s_tests.detail: phi is excluded by construction: its offset is the allowed gauge constant, not a discrepancy

task2s_tests.purpose: the k = 0 reduced answer is the limit of the k > 0 answer, which is what makes the row removal legitimate
task2s_tests.oracle: the production assembly at k = 1e-2, 1e-3, 1e-4 k_ac, reduced against the k = 0 answer by extrapolation, not by assumption
task2s_tests.expected: relative change in the transfer ratio falls by a factor near 10 per decade of k, i.e. first order
task2s_tests.tol_justification: first-order approach gives a ratio of 10; the tolerance is 2.0 for the ratio itself, allowing a generous 5x band, because the limit is checked structurally (monotone, decade-scaling) rather than against a fitted constant
task2s_tests.detail: extrapolation in k is an oracle independent of the k = 0 row-removal rule

task2s_tests.purpose: the interface electrical model is explicit in the record, and the removed Dz row is identified as the insulated condition
task2s_tests.oracle: the system's own removal reasons and kept-row list, checked against the derivation: bonded => phi continuity, insulated => D_z continuity
task2s_tests.fixture: all four pairs at k = 0, both polarisations
task2s_tests.expected: at k = 0 exactly the electrical rows are removed, D_z is among them (it is the insulated condition and must not be imposed on a bonded contact), and every mechanical and thermal row is kept
task2s_tests.actual: only the electrical rows are removed at k = 0, D_z is removed in every configuration (the insulated row must NOT be imposed on a bonded contact), and every mechanical/thermal row survives. Al6061|Al6061 P: removed=['phi', 'Dz']; Al6061|Al6061 SV: removed=['phi', 'Dz']; PZT-5H|PZT-5H P: removed=['Dz']
task2s_tests.detail: the classification comes from the derivation: bonded => phi continuity, insulated => D_z continuity, and at k = 0 the D_z row IS the insulated condition

task2s_tests.purpose: the reduced system's rank and residual are stable from 30 to 100 decimal digits, so the conclusion is not a precision artefact
task2s_tests.oracle: re-solving the same matrix at five working precisions; a genuine rank deficiency would persist or move, a numerical one would improve with digits
task2s_tests.fixture: Al|PZT and PZT|Al at k = 0, SV
task2s_tests.expected: rank equals the column count at every precision, residual falls with precision, condition number stays below 1e8
task2s_tests.tol_justification: the weakest precision tested is 30 digits; the residual bound is set there and must be met by all
task2s_tests.actual: dps=30 rank=6 res=9.9e-32 cond=1.1e+3; dps=30 rank=6 res=0.0 cond=1.1e+3; dps=40 rank=6 res=0.0 cond=1.1e+3; dps=40 rank=6 res=0.0 cond=1.1e+3 ...
task2s_tests.detail: a real deficiency would not vanish as digits are added; this one is absent at the lowest precision already

precision_sweep.rank_value: 6/6 for every pair at every dps
precision_sweep.conclusion: rank does not move with precision and residual falls with it, so the full rank is not a precision artefact
